turns.t: Hello, doctor. I came to check my coil, because I can't feel the strings anymore.
I'm her sister, I came along for support. She's been worried about it for a week. ~
That's perfectly reasonable. When did you last feel the strings?
I think about a month ago. Maybe six weeks. I'm not sure, I don't check very often.
When was the coil fitted?
Three years ago. It's the hormone one, the levonorgestrel coil.
Have you had any pain, unusual bleeding, or discharge?
No pain, no bleeding, no discharge. Just the missing strings.
When was your last period? ~
I don't really get them with the coil. Just a light spotting now and then. ~
Is there any chance you could be pregnant? ~
I took a test last week, and it was negative. ~
Good. What other medicines are you taking?
A thyroid tablet, levothyroxine, 75 micrograms in the morning. Iron tablets, 200 mg, once a day. And paracetamol, 500 mg, now and then.
Thank you. Any past medical problems?
Underactive thyroid, and I'm anaemic.
Any operations in the past?
A caesarean section, seven years ago.
Thank you. My colleague will check your blood pressure and pulse first. ~
Please sit and relax your arm. ~
Okay.
Blood pressure 110 over 70, pulse 72.
Those are good. Now I'll do a speculum examination and look for the strings. ~
Okay. Please be gentle.
I can see the strings. They're short, and tucked up in the canal, but they are there.
Oh, thank God. So it's in place? ~
It seems to be in place, yes. Strings sometimes curl up and are hard to feel.
So she doesn't need it removed? ~
No. I'd still like to arrange a scan to confirm the position, because it's three years since it was fitted.
When would that be? ~
Within two weeks. You'll get a letter. If it's in the right place, nothing more is needed. ~
That's a relief. ~
Until the scan, use condoms in case it has moved, and come back if you get pain or bleeding.
I will. Thank you both. ~
